purpose: Safety, provenance and human-control boundaries for exercise logging, programme assistance and workout companion features.
requirements: Workout, programme and measurement records are scoped to the authenticated owner and selected participant.
Health and measurement imports are bounded, schema validated, unit constrained and reject non-finite or implausible values.
Recorded workouts, targets and measurements are distinguished from inferred progress, readiness, technique or clinical status.
AI coaching receives only the selected workout/programme context and treats saved records and reference material as untrusted data rather than instructions.
AI responses cannot directly mutate programmes, workout logs or health records; proposed changes require deterministic application validation and explicit user review.
Slow AI operations bind their result to the exact reviewed record revision so concurrent changes invalidate stale advice or drafts.
Exercise alternatives based on movement or equipment similarity are not represented as evidence of clinical suitability.
Pain, injury, rehabilitation, medication or conflicting practitioner instructions trigger a bounded response that does not diagnose, clear return-to-activity or replace professional care.
Recorded practitioner restrictions retain provenance and cannot be silently loosened or removed by model output.
Load progression, maximum-effort attempts and personalised rehabilitation are not autonomously prescribed from incomplete workout history.
Minor participants receive age-appropriate safeguards against restrictive dieting, appearance judgement, performance-enhancing-drug advice and aggressive progression.
Model/provider storage is disabled when supported for private exercise interactions, with bounded request/output sizes and explicit provider failures.
When participant identity, record revision, health context or safety constraints cannot be established, affected coaching or programme mutations fail closed.
nonClaims: This policy does not make the application a doctor, physiotherapist or personal trainer.
This policy does not establish that an exercise is medically safe for a particular person.
This policy does not infer good technique, recovery or progress from logged data alone.
This policy does not replace emergency or professional medical assessment.
